What actually binds is the canon absorbed fraction 4e-5: at the mission power the drive share allows 4e-5 of the fusion power into hardware.

fiji.note: 1.6A: field-following (SEEDED, the one property) adds at most 3 % of the stop field; ORIENTED needs coercivity at 1000 K (a second property). FG-2 adds about 1.1 kt per engine.

animation.note: One DRIVE_MANIFOLD_CTRL object drives per-engine effects through Blender drivers that the viewer evaluates (vertex_cluster.drivers / display); named states OFF..SHUTDOWN. No moving engine part and no Godot mechanism binding exists for the engines (the export is static).

verdict.statement: The exhaust reaches L2 in 396 ns; a 1 km/s rim moves 0.40 mm in that time and a segmented crown modulates the field at 4.0e-03 of the mission pulse rate. Motion can only set the geometry between pulses (quasi-static); it cannot shape a pulse. Electronic switching is 10-100 times faster than the transit, a superconducting coil is not (it needs ~1e8 V to follow a pulse), and the flux the pulse compresses into the static coils is already the lossless dynamic coupling.

crown.field_change: none: the crown field is axisymmetric at every instant; rotation adds nothing a static ring does not give
crown.fiji: 1.6A: a field-following (SEEDED) lattice aligns with the local field whatever the crown angle, so turning it changes nothing; ORIENTED magnetization would need coercivity (a second property).
crown.heat: axisymmetric engine: the burn load is uniform in azimuth, so turning about the engine axis spreads nothing
crown.verdict: REJECT for the drive: no field, confinement or heat benefit; it adds ~92 t per pair, burst energy, gyroscopic loads and a synchronization failure mode. Kept only as a negative result.

thermodynamics.statement: Fiji works between 550 and 1100 K, below the 1800 K radiators: its heat must be pumped up (cost 3.12 radiator W per W). Converting a share of it to work removes at most that share; it can never lower the heat that reaches the radiators below what rejecting at the hot end would need (a heat engine feeding a radiator needs area (Th/Tc)^3 >= 1 times the direct rejection).

dynamo.verdict: KEEP TWO SMALL PARTS: (1) an ignition bootstrap store (flywheel motor-generator) that charges the pulse pods for the first pulses until direct conversion of the burn feeds the driver; (2) leadless persistent coils (HTS dynamo or retractable leads). Rejected: storage for sustained or kHz power, a separate coil-charging store (the coils are the 9.7 GJ SMES), switched pulse coils (they would have to recover all but 5e-5 of the pulse energy) and the Fiji heat engine.

petals.vectoring: cluster differential throttle already gives 17.4 MN m per engine (LC-06); petal tilt is not needed for steering
petals.evidence: SCALING_ESTIMATE: self-similar field scaling at the 1.3 stop rule, not a field or plasma solution; the capture and leakage of a deployed nozzle are assumed unchanged (self-similar ideal MHD) and stay OPEN
petals.verdict: KEEP as the geometry lever: deployed to k 1.40 (the cluster spacing allows 1.41) the coils take 79% of their sky and 51% of their fluence; field energy unchanged, loop forces /1.40, inter-engine pull x2.7; +193 t per engine (hinges, longer conductor). Static during the burn.

tread.angular_momentum: zero by symmetry (poloidal circulation; the local moments point along the ring and cancel)
tread.verdict: KEEP: a real, bounded gain (peak flux /pi, renewable surface, a shadow-side radiating face); total heat is unchanged and the added sink is a few per cent of the drive share at most.

neutrons.note: a few collisions with protons are needed to absorb a neutron

propellant.trapping_1_6b: 1.6B: dense-target Compton trapping lowers photons at most 3.3x
propellant.verdict: The propellant of one pulse forms an absorbing layer only within millimetres of the burn, which is the target itself (already in the 1.6B source). A shell at 1 m would add hundreds of kg per pulse and cut the exhaust speed by orders of magnitude; absorbed energy also leaves isotropically, not as thrust.

cold.note: 1.6B: unshielded REBCO lasts ~1 s at mission power; deployment buys a factor ~2, shields still 43-45 kt

plasma.note: Charged leakage (1.4 ledger) dominates the best 1.6B budget. Motion cannot act in the ~100 ns transit; magnetic shielding of walls (Hall thrusters) reduced erosion by 2-3 orders in a much gentler plasma.

source.note: unchanged: no mechanism here changes the burn physics (1.6B); a quieter source is a separate speculative principle (SP-17B)

driver.note: Not in the 1.6B ledger: the driver of an inertial burn draws Pf/(G eta) and its losses and the conversion losses that feed it are rejected at loss_K. Shown at the optimistic bracket (G 100, eta 0.5, conversion 0.9).

budget.note: Ratios are radiator watts over the drive share per engine (all four engines alike). Only the deposition geometry, the added sinks and the leakage term change; the source, jet, thrust and exhaust speed are the 1.6B mission point.

mission.note: Thrust, exhaust speed and burn time stay at the B01 point; added mass lowers the acceleration in proportion (power-limited burn) and must fit the departure margin, or the tanks grow.

sequence.description: Fusion off; petals folded and latched, treads parked, dynamos still, coils at zero current.
Latches release, petals swing out to the deployed radius, treads start; the dynamo rotors spin up.
The dynamos pump current into the coils (no leads) until the stop field stands; persistent switches close; dynamos stop.
Lattice heated through activation (650 K) to its operating point (1000 K); its response rises.
Driver pulse train; first burns; the treads reach running speed as the lit faces heat.
Petals locked, coils persistent, treads circulating, trim coils holding the plume; no other motion.
Throttle changes pulse rate; tread speed follows the lit heat; trim coils steer; diagonal pairs balance torque.
Pulses stop; treads run on while the faces cool; Fiji falls below release; coils ramp down by the dynamos run backwards or stay persistent; petals fold after cool-down.
See the failure table: the visible cue is the mechanism that failed (a stopped tread glows, a petal off its latch, a quench vent).

verdict.statement: The recommended hybrid lowers the mission-point radiator ratio from 6,720 to 6,619 (x1.02); counting the driver recirculation this audit adds, 7,688. Mechanical motion acts on seconds to minutes; the gap is set by a ~100 ns plasma capture (leakage), by the source and by the driver gain, so no moving assembly can close it. Closing needs SP-17A, SP-17B and SP-17D together, each beyond any precedent.

answers.q: Does rotation make a useful field?
answers.a: No. An axisymmetric crown turned about its axis makes the same field; segments add a 3.9e-03 ripple at half radius at ~117 Hz.

answers.q: Is motion fast enough for the plasma?
answers.a: No: 4.0e-03 of the pulse rate; rotating-field current drive needs 1e+05 times faster rotation than any rim.
No: one second of mission power needs 327 kt of flywheel. A flywheel can bootstrap ignition (10 pulses at 1 Hz: 58 t nominal); the coils themselves already store their 9.7 GJ.

answers.q: Does a Fiji thermomagnetic cycle help?
answers.a: No: about 1.8% of the heat at best, and Fiji works below the radiator temperature.
Deployed petals (coil sky x0.79, fluence x0.51), treads (peak flux /pi) and leadless HTS dynamos: real but bounded.
Barely: x1.02, because charged leakage dominates the best budget.
Near-perfect capture (SP-17A; even zero leakage leaves 112x), a 180x quieter source (SP-17B) and a target gain near 108,401 (SP-17D), all at once.
No: every kept part adds mass; the static engine is already outside the canon mass budget.
